newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, follow soft U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, follow soft U.S. bonds.

text.p: Canada's bond market ended weaker on Tuesday, depressed by a softer U.S. market despite a firmer Canadian dollar earlier in the day.

"The focus of the markets Tuesday centered around the strengthening of the (Canadian dollar) attributed to technical factors and the continued effects of the U.S. market," Technical Data analyst David Ebata said in a market report.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond dipped C$0.28 to C$110.62 to yield 7.100 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark, which lost 13/32 to yield 6.85 percent. The spread remained at 25 basis points from the close of trading on Monday.
The Canadian dollar ended firmer at C$1.3670 (US$0.7315) from opening levels on Tuesday, but gave up some of its early gains after a flurry of buying interest petered out.
U.S. and Canadian bond markets adopted a defensive mood ahead of Wednesday's release of the Beige Book numbers.
"People are a little bit reluctant to get too excited," said TD Securities Inc analyst Richard Wylie.
"For the most part, we followed the U.S. today," he said.
U.S. bond investors continued to debate the probability and timing of a hike in short-term U.S. interest rates.
